label: preparing
what: A coordinated jubilee or hospitality gathering in the great hall at eighteen, with roughly two hundred loaves delivered into table chests and newly installed lighting. The innkeeper and baker call it jubilee bread but describe the mayor's attendance only as a lighting inspection, suggesting a concealed celebration. Freight finances supplies and hauls bread; innkeeper commissions and arranges payment. Secretary schedules the inspection and bringing the mayor; builder supplies the lighting inspection. Their knowing involvement in a concealed celebration, rather than merely the stated inspection, is not established.
